items.originalTitle: Heysel 85 review – rage-filled denunciation of the incompetence that fuelled a football disaster
items.author: Peter Bradshaw
items.title: Heysel 85 review – rage-filled denunciation of the incompetence that fuelled a football disaster
items.summary: Teodora Ana Mihai and her passionately committed cast reconstruct the grim sequence of bad judgments that led to 39 fans dying Shame and rage are the keynotes of this immersive, viscerally powerful drama-thriller set amid the macabre tragedy of football’s 1985 European Cup final between Juventus and Liverpool in the crumbling Heysel stadium in Brussels. Crowd disorder before kickoff in a poorly maintained, badly policed venue resulted in the deaths of 39 fans. In this film, the roar of the crowd echoing overhead through the stadium’s claustrophobic tunnels is like the wailing of the damned, while the sport’s officer class flinch and panic as if at a wartime loss. Grimly, the match was allowed to go ahead, despite the fatalities; the authorities believed the game itself would restore order on a bread-and-circuses basis, and that abandoning the match would only cause greater violence and chaos. Heysel 85 is directed and co-written by Romanian-born and Belgian-based film-maker Teodora Ana Mihai; she is a former collaborator of Cristian Mungiu, though maybe the influence here is more Paul Greengrass. The film-makers have been criticised for fictionalising aspects: the players are depicted as not being aware that fans had died before they took to the field – they were in fact largely aware, although it may well be true that the slippery authorities sought to minimise the truth as much as they could. And the fictionalised mayor of Brussels, here named Marc Dumont (Josse De Pauw), has been criticised as an unfair drunken caricature of the actual mayor, Hervé Brouhon.

items.originalTitle: The pest I’ll never forget: the bedbugs that bit me – and worried Jake Gyllenhaal
items.author: Catherine Shoard
items.title: The pest I’ll never forget: the bedbugs that bit me – and worried Jake Gyllenhaal
items.summary: An infestation at my hotel meant my clothes had to be fumigated. When I turned up in shorts to interview the actor, he lent me his jacket, but I suspect he may have regretted it The biting flies were wild in Toronto in September 2012. A colleague and I were there to cover the film festival, but our key reference that year was a zinger from the 2007 cartoon Bee Movie, when it turns out Chris Rock’s mosquito has become a lawyer: “I was already a bloodsucking parasite,” he says, “all I needed was a briefcase!” (Bee Movie is one of the most brilliant and adult children’s movies ever; its central premise compares the honey industry to concentration camps.) Anyway, I spent the first week getting ever more bloodless and lumpy. We even shot a video about them, spraying repellent in front of us like Mace. It didn’t work. Every morning I woke bumpier than before.
